## 0. Context, goal, and non-negotiable rules

Creativity ratings on a unipolar 7-point scale (1 = not creative, 7 = very creative) are available for approximately 4,000 football actions. The number of ratings per action is unequal (roughly 600 actions with one rating, roughly 2,000 with two ratings, the rest with three to seven ratings). Not all raters rated the same actions — the design is **unbalanced, incomplete, and (partially) crossed**.

This notebook implements the R counterparts of the Python approach notebooks (`02a_classical_consensus`, `02b_linear_mixed_model`, `02c_ordinal_facet_model`, `02d_judge_response_theory`, `03_approach_comparison`), with R-specific advantages: `lme4` estimates the linear crossed model for \~4,000 action levels natively and quickly (sparse Cholesky factorization), where `statsmodels.MixedLM` in Python does not scale in practice (see `02b_linear_mixed_model.ipynb`, Section 2.2); `brms` provides the Bayesian ordinal facette modeling via Stan; the dedicated CRAN package `jrt` is used for the judge-response-theory extension, if installed.

### Non-negotiable rules (from the analysis brief)

-   Absolute agreement ≠ relative consistency ≠ reliability of a single rating ≠ reliability of an aggregated score.
-   Actions with only one rating are kept for model-based estimation but contribute no within-action agreement information.
-   Rater severity is only identifiable within connected components of the rater–action graph.
-   No action score without the number of ratings and an uncertainty statement.
-   Interpretation is cautious, descriptive, without mechanical good/bad thresholds.

### Data used in this run

This notebook reads the already-cleaned rating data produced by `00_data_loading_preprocessing.ipynb` (`data/processed/ratings_long_clean.csv`). That notebook is the single place where the Google Sheets export is downloaded and cleaned; run it first if the file is missing or stale.

### References

Amabile (1982, 1996); Baayen, Davidson & Bates (2008); Bates, Mächler, Bolker & Walker (2015); Brennan (2001); Bürkner (2017); Eckes (2015); Krippendorff (2004/2018); Linacre (1989); Myszkowski & Storme (2019); Myszkowski (2021, R package `jrt`); Primi, Silvia, Jauk & Benedek (2019); Shavelson & Webb (1991); Shrout & Fleiss (1979); McGraw & Wong (1996); Koo & Li (2016). Full citations: see `../APPROACHES.md`. Software documentation: current `lme4`, `brms`, `jrt`, `krippendorffsalpha` documentation (see the respective CRAN pages).

## 3. Data overview and plausibility checks

### LMM Baseline

#### Check Rater-Stimulus-Graph
```{r}
library(igraph)
g <- graph_from_data_frame(df[, c("action_id", "rater_id")], directed = FALSE)
components(g)$no  # sollte 1 sein – sonst zerfällt das Linking in unverbundene Teilnetze
```

#### LMM

```{r}
library(lme4)

m_lmm <- lmer(rating ~ 1 + (1 | action_id) + (1 | rater_id), data = df)
summary(m_lmm)
```

```{r}
# Varianzkomponenten: Stimulus-Signal vs. Rater-Strenge vs. Residuum
VarCorr(m_lmm)

# "Fair average" pro Stimulus = Intercept + BLUP (shrinkage-korrigiert)
fair_lmm <- coef(m_lmm)$action_id[, "(Intercept)"]
```


### Many-Facet Rasch Model

```{r}
library(sirt)
dat_mat <- matrix(df$rating, ncol = 1, dimnames = list(NULL, "creativity"))

mod_mfrm <- sirt::rm.facets(
  dat   = dat_mat,
  pid   = df$action_id,
  rater = df$rater_id
)

summary(mod_mfrm)

theta_mfrm <- mod_mfrm$person$theta      # Stimulus-Fähigkeit (logit)
sev_mfrm   <- mod_mfrm$rater$b.rater     # Rater-severity

mod_mfrm$rater.se   # oder je nach sirt-Version: mod_mfrm$rater.se, prüfe str(mod_mfrm)
```
### Judge Response Theory

#### Rohes MIRT package

```{r}
library(mirt)
df_wide[] <- lapply(df_wide |> select(-action_id), ordered)
mod_mirt <- mirt(df_wide, model = 1, itemtype = "graded", SE = TRUE)
```


#### JRT package (kein NA-handling)

```{r}
library(jrt)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)

df_wide <- df |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = action_id, names_from = rater_id, values_from = rating)

# jrt() bekommt nur die Judge-Spalten, ohne die ID-Spalte
mod_jrt <- jrt(df_wide |> select(-action_id))


summary(mod_jrt)
plot(mod_jrt)  # gibt u.a. Rater-Diskrimination und -Schwellenwerte grafisch aus

# a = discrimination pro Rater, b1..bk = Schwellenwerte
coef(mod_jrt, IRTpars = TRUE, simplify = TRUE)

# latente Kreativitäts-Scores (theta) inkl. Standardfehler
scores_jrt <- fscores(mod_jrt, full.scores.SE = TRUE)
```



















### 3.3 Temporal drift (descriptive)

```{r drift-descriptive}

if ("rating_order" %in% names(df)) {
  drift_corr <- df %>%
    group_by(rater_id) %>%

  save_table(drift_corr, "descriptive_drift_correlation_by_rater_R")
} else {

}

ratings_clean <- df
```

## 4. Connectivity and identifiability

As in `01_data_overview.ipynb`: bipartite rater–action graph, connected components. Rater severity is only interpretable on a common scale within a single component.

```{r connectivity}

edges <- ratings_clean %>%
  transmute(action = action_id, rater = paste0("R::", rater_id)) %>%
  as.matrix()

g <- graph_from_edgelist(edges, directed = FALSE)
V(g)$type <- grepl("^R::", V(g)$name)  # TRUE = rater node

comp <- components(g)
comp_sizes <- sort(table(comp$membership), decreasing = TRUE)
n_components <- comp$no

comp_summary <- tibble(component_id = seq_len(n_components)) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    nodes_in_comp = list(V(g)$name[comp$membership == component_id]),
    n_nodes = length(nodes_in_comp),
    n_actions = sum(!grepl("^R::", nodes_in_comp)),
    n_raters = sum(grepl("^R::", nodes_in_comp))
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(desc(n_nodes)) %>%
  select(-nodes_in_comp)

save_table(comp_summary, "connectivity_component_summary_R")
print(comp_summary)

cat("\nNumber of connected components:", n_components, "\n")
if (n_components > 1) {
  log_warning(sprintf(paste(
    "The rater-action graph has %d separate components. Rater severity from",
    "different components is NOT comparable on a common scale.",
    "The main analysis uses the largest component."), n_components))
}

largest_comp_id <- as.integer(names(comp_sizes)[1])
largest_component_nodes <- V(g)$name[comp$membership == largest_comp_id]
largest_component_actions <- largest_component_nodes[!grepl("^R::", largest_component_nodes)]
largest_component_raters <- sub("^R::", "", largest_component_nodes[grepl("^R::", largest_component_nodes)])

action_component_map <- tibble(action_id = V(g)$name[!V(g)$type],
                                 connected_component = comp$membership[!V(g)$type] - 1L)
# component_id 0 = largest component (same convention as in the Python notebooks)
main_id <- comp$membership[largest_component_nodes[1]]
action_component_map <- action_component_map %>%
  mutate(connected_component = if_else(comp$membership[match(action_id, V(g)$name)] == main_id, 0L, 1L))

ratings_clean <- ratings_clean %>%
  left_join(action_component_map, by = "action_id") %>%
  mutate(in_largest_component = connected_component == 0)

cat(sprintf("\nLargest component: %d actions, %d raters (%.1f%% of all actions)\n",
             length(largest_component_actions), length(largest_component_raters),
             100 * length(largest_component_actions) / n_distinct(ratings_clean$action_id)))
```

> **Interpretation:** rater severity parameters are only identifiable relative to other raters if the rating design is sufficiently connected. All rater-correcting models below are estimated on the largest connected component; actions outside it receive a corresponding `score_flag` in `action_scores.csv`.

```{r connectivity-overlap}

rater_ids_sorted <- sort(unique(ratings_clean$rater_id))
n_raters <- length(rater_ids_sorted)

action_to_raters <- ratings_clean %>% group_by(action_id) %>% summarise(raters = list(rater_id))
overlap <- matrix(0L, n_raters, n_raters, dimnames = list(rater_ids_sorted, rater_ids_sorted))
for (rs in action_to_raters$raters) {
  if (length(rs) < 2) next
  idx <- match(unique(rs), rater_ids_sorted)
  for (a in seq_along(idx)) for (b in seq_along(idx)) if (a != b) overlap[idx[a], idx[b]] <- overlap[idx[a], idx[b]] + 1L
}
overlap_df <- as_tibble(overlap, rownames = "rater_id")
save_table(overlap_df, "rater_pair_overlap_matrix_R")

pair_overlaps <- overlap[upper.tri(overlap)]
pair_overlaps_nonzero <- pair_overlaps[pair_overlaps > 0]

overlap_long <- as_tibble(overlap, rownames = "rater_1") %>%
  pivot_longer(-rater_1, names_to = "rater_2", values_to = "n_common")
p_heat <- ggplot(overlap_long, aes(x = rater_1, y = rater_2, fill = n_common)) +
  geom_tile() + scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  theme_minimal() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, size = 5), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 5)) +
  labs(title = "Heatmap: jointly rated actions per rater pair", x = NULL, y = NULL)
save_fig(p_heat, "fig05_rater_overlap_heatmap_R", width = 8, height = 7,
          caption = "Heatmap of jointly rated actions per rater pair.")
p_heat

mean_pair_overlap <- tibble(
  rater_id = rater_ids_sorted,
  mean_pair_overlap = rowSums(overlap) / pmax(1, rowSums(overlap > 0))
)
cat("Median overlap (rater pairs>0):", median(pair_overlaps_nonzero), "\n")
cat("Share of rater pairs with no shared action:",
    scales::percent(mean(pair_overlaps == 0)), "\n")
```

## 5. Descriptive pairwise agreement

```{r pairwise-agreement}

MIN_OVERLAP <- 10

wide <- ratings_clean %>%
  select(action_id, rater_id, rating_numeric) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = rater_id, values_from = rating_numeric)

pair_stats <- list()
rater_cols <- setdiff(names(wide), "action_id")
for (i in seq_along(rater_cols)) {
  for (j in seq_along(rater_cols)) {
    if (j <= i) next
    rj <- rater_cols[i]; rk <- rater_cols[j]
    both <- wide %>% select(all_of(c(rj, rk))) %>% drop_na()
    n_common <- nrow(both)
    if (n_common < MIN_OVERLAP) next
    yj <- both[[rj]]; yk <- both[[rk]]
    w_kappa <- irr::kappa2(cbind(yj, yk), weight = "squared")$value
    pair_stats[[length(pair_stats) + 1]] <- tibble(
      rater_1 = rj, rater_2 = rk, n_common_actions = n_common,
      pearson_r = cor(yj, yk, method = "pearson"),
      spearman_r = cor(yj, yk, method = "spearman"),
      kendall_tau = cor(yj, yk, method = "kendall"),
      mean_diff_1_minus_2 = mean(yj - yk),
      sd_diff = sd(yj - yk),
      mae = mean(abs(yj - yk)),
      weighted_kappa = w_kappa
    )
  }
}
pair_stats_df <- bind_rows(pair_stats)
save_table(pair_stats_df, "pairwise_rater_agreement_R")
cat(sprintf("Rater pairs with >= %d shared actions: %d of %d possible pairs\n",
             MIN_OVERLAP, nrow(pair_stats_df), n_raters * (n_raters - 1) / 2))
summary(pair_stats_df)
```

```{r bland-altman}

top_pairs <- pair_stats_df %>% slice_max(n_common_actions, n = 2)
ba_plots <- pmap(top_pairs, function(rater_1, rater_2, ...) {
  both <- wide %>% select(all_of(c(rater_1, rater_2))) %>% drop_na()
  m <- rowMeans(both); d <- both[[rater_1]] - both[[rater_2]]
  md <- mean(d); sdd <- sd(d)
  ggplot(tibble(m = m, d = d), aes(m, d)) +
    geom_jitter(width = 0.05, height = 0.05, alpha = 0.3, color = "#4C72B0") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = md) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = md + 1.96 * sdd, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = md - 1.96 * sdd, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
    labs(title = sprintf("%s vs %s (n=%d)", rater_1, rater_2, nrow(both)),
          x = "Mean of both ratings", y = "Difference") +
    theme_minimal()
})
fig_ba <- gridExtra_or_patchwork(ba_plots[[1]], ba_plots[[2]])
save_fig(fig_ba, "fig06_bland_altman_top_pairs_R", width = 11, height = 4.5,
          caption = "Bland-Altman-style plots for the two rater pairs with the strongest overlap.")
fig_ba
```

## 6. Krippendorff's alpha

Primarily **ordinal** alpha (category distances not assumed equal), plus **interval-scaled** alpha as a sensitivity analysis. Preferred package: `krippendorffsalpha` (reliability-data matrix: raters × units, `NA` = missing).

```{r krippendorff-alpha}

reliability_data <- t(as.matrix(wide %>% select(-action_id)))

if (has_pkg("krippendorffsalpha")) {
  alpha_ordinal <- krippendorffsalpha::krippendorffs.alpha(
    reliability_data, level = "ordinal", confint = FALSE)$alpha.hat
  alpha_interval <- krippendorffsalpha::krippendorffs.alpha(
    reliability_data, level = "interval", confint = FALSE)$alpha.hat
} else {
  log_warning("Package 'krippendorffsalpha' not available - using irr::kripp.alpha as a substitute (less flexible with missing values).")
  alpha_ordinal <- irr::kripp.alpha(reliability_data, method = "ordinal")$value
  alpha_interval <- irr::kripp.alpha(reliability_data, method = "interval")$value
}

cat(sprintf("Krippendorff's alpha (ordinal, primary):       %.3f\n", alpha_ordinal))
cat(sprintf("Krippendorff's alpha (interval, sensitivity):  %.3f\n", alpha_interval))
```

### 6.1 Uncertainty: cluster bootstrap over actions

```{r krippendorff-bootstrap}

N_BOOT <- 2000
action_ids_all <- wide$action_id
n_actions_all <- length(action_ids_all)
set.seed(SEED)

alpha_fun <- function(rel_data) {
  if (has_pkg("krippendorffsalpha")) {
    list(
      ord = krippendorffsalpha::krippendorffs.alpha(rel_data, level = "ordinal", confint = FALSE)$alpha.hat,
      int = krippendorffsalpha::krippendorffs.alpha(rel_data, level = "interval", confint = FALSE)$alpha.hat
    )
  } else {
    list(ord = irr::kripp.alpha(rel_data, method = "ordinal")$value,
          int = irr::kripp.alpha(rel_data, method = "interval")$value)
  }
}

boot_alphas <- map(seq_len(N_BOOT), function(b) {
  sampled <- sample(action_ids_all, n_actions_all, replace = TRUE)
  boot_wide <- wide[match(sampled, wide$action_id), ]
  rel <- t(as.matrix(boot_wide %>% select(-action_id)))
  tryCatch(alpha_fun(rel), error = function(e) list(ord = NA_real_, int = NA_real_))
})
boot_ord <- map_dbl(boot_alphas, "ord")
boot_int <- map_dbl(boot_alphas, "int")

ci_ord <- quantile(boot_ord, c(.025, .975), na.rm = TRUE)
ci_int <- quantile(boot_int, c(.025, .975), na.rm = TRUE)
cat(sprintf("Ordinal alpha: %.3f, 95%% CI [%.3f, %.3f] (n_boot=%d, %d failed)\n",
             alpha_ordinal, ci_ord[1], ci_ord[2], N_BOOT, sum(is.na(boot_ord))))
cat(sprintf("Interval alpha: %.3f, 95%% CI [%.3f, %.3f]\n", alpha_interval, ci_int[1], ci_int[2]))

alpha_summary_df <- tibble(
  measure = c("ordinal", "interval"),
  alpha = c(alpha_ordinal, alpha_interval),
  ci_low = c(ci_ord[1], ci_int[1]), ci_high = c(ci_ord[2], ci_int[2]), n_boot = N_BOOT
)
save_table(alpha_summary_df, "krippendorff_alpha_main_R")
```

### 6.2 Subgroup sensitivity

```{r krippendorff-subgroups}

alpha_for_subset <- function(action_subset, label) {
  sub_wide <- wide %>% filter(action_id %in% action_subset)
  rel <- t(as.matrix(sub_wide %>% select(-action_id)))
  a <- alpha_fun(rel)
  tibble(subset = label, n_actions = nrow(sub_wide), alpha_ordinal = a$ord, alpha_interval = a$int)
}

subset_results <- bind_rows(
  alpha_for_subset(wide$action_id, "all actions"),
  alpha_for_subset(ratings_per_action$action_id[ratings_per_action$n_ratings >= 2], "n_ratings >= 2"),
  alpha_for_subset(ratings_per_action$action_id[ratings_per_action$n_ratings >= 3], "n_ratings >= 3"),
  alpha_for_subset(largest_component_actions, "largest connected component")
)
save_table(subset_results, "krippendorff_alpha_sensitivity_R")
print(subset_results)
log_warning("Krippendorff's alpha values from different subsets are not directly comparable due to differing action heterogeneity.")
```

## 7. Linear crossed mixed-effects model

$$
y_{ij} = \mu + u_i + v_j + \varepsilon_{ij}, \quad
u_i \sim \mathcal N(0,\sigma^2_{\text{action}}), \quad
v_j \sim \mathcal N(0,\sigma^2_{\text{rater}}), \quad
\varepsilon_{ij} \sim \mathcal N(0,\sigma^2_e)
$$

Unlike `statsmodels.MixedLM` in Python (see the discussion there, Section 6.2: `vc_formula` does not scale practically to \~4,000 action levels due to dense design matrices), `lme4::lmer` estimates this model **natively and quickly** via sparse Cholesky factorization, even with thousands of levels. We estimate on the largest connected component.

```{r lmm-fit}

df_lmm <- ratings_clean %>% filter(in_largest_component)

model_lmm <- lmer(
  rating_numeric ~ 1 + (1 | action_id) + (1 | rater_id),
  data = df_lmm, REML = TRUE,
  control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
)
summary(model_lmm)

is_singular <- isSingular(model_lmm)
cat("\nSingularity check:", ifelse(is_singular, "SINGULAR", "ok"), "\n")
if (is_singular) log_warning("lmer fit is singular (at least one variance component ~0).")
if (has_pkg("performance")) {
  print(performance::check_convergence(model_lmm))
}
```

```{r lmm-varcomp}

vc <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(model_lmm))
var_action <- vc$vcov[vc$grp == "action_id"]
var_rater <- vc$vcov[vc$grp == "rater_id"]
var_resid <- vc$vcov[vc$grp == "Residual"]

variance_components_df <- tibble(
  component = c("action (u_i)", "rater (v_j)", "residual (eps_ij)"),
  variance = c(var_action, var_rater, var_resid)
) %>% mutate(pct_of_total = variance / sum(variance))
save_table(variance_components_df, "lmm_variance_components_R")
print(variance_components_df)
stopifnot(all(variance_components_df$variance >= 0))
```

### 7.1 BLUPs (conditional modes)

```{r lmm-blups}

re <- ranef(model_lmm, condVar = TRUE)
action_blup <- as_tibble(re$action_id, rownames = "action_id") %>%
  rename(lmm_score_deviation = `(Intercept)`)
rater_blup <- as_tibble(re$rater_id, rownames = "rater_id") %>%
  rename(lmm_severity = `(Intercept)`)

# extract conditional SDs from postVar
action_postvar <- attr(re$action_id, "postVar")
action_blup$lmm_score_se <- sqrt(action_postvar[1, 1, ])
rater_postvar <- attr(re$rater_id, "postVar")
rater_blup$lmm_severity_se <- sqrt(rater_postvar[1, 1, ])

mu_hat <- fixef(model_lmm)[["(Intercept)"]]
cat("Fixed intercept (grand mean):", round(mu_hat, 3), "\n")
save_table(action_blup, "lmm_action_blups_R")
save_table(rater_blup, "lmm_rater_blups_R")
```

### 7.2 Absolute and relative reliability, D-study

$$
\rho_{\text{abs},k} = \frac{\sigma^2_{\text{action}}}{\sigma^2_{\text{action}}+\sigma^2_{\text{rater}}/k+\sigma^2_e/k}, \qquad
\rho_{\text{rel},k} = \frac{\sigma^2_{\text{action}}}{\sigma^2_{\text{action}}+\sigma^2_e/k}
$$

### 7.3 Uncertainty: parametric bootstrap (`lme4::bootMer`)

**Note on compute time:** `bootMer` with `nsim=200` refits the model 200 times; with \~4,000 action levels this can take several minutes depending on the machine. For a quick test run, reduce `nsim` (e.g. to 20) and increase it back to ≥200 before the final publication run.

```{r lmm-dstudy-bootstrap}

reliability_abs <- function(k, va, vr, ve) va / (va + vr / k + ve / k)
reliability_rel <- function(k, va, ve) va / (va + ve / k)

N_BOOT_LMM <- 200  # reduce for a quick test run if needed

extract_vc <- function(fit) {
  vc_b <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(fit))
  c(va = vc_b$vcov[vc_b$grp == "action_id"],
     vr = vc_b$vcov[vc_b$grp == "rater_id"],
     ve = vc_b$vcov[vc_b$grp == "Residual"])
}

boot_result <- tryCatch(
  bootMer(model_lmm, FUN = extract_vc, nsim = N_BOOT_LMM, seed = SEED,
           use.u = FALSE, type = "parametric",
           .progress = "none"),
  error = function(e) { log_warning(paste("bootMer failed:", conditionMessage(e))); NULL }
)

if (!is.null(boot_result)) {
  boot_vc_df <- as_tibble(boot_result$t) %>% setNames(c("va", "vr", "ve")) %>% drop_na()
  boot_vc_df <- boot_vc_df %>% mutate(
    rho_abs_1 = va / (va + vr + ve),
    rho_rel_1 = va / (va + ve)
  )
  vc_ci <- tibble(
    quantity = c("sigma2_action", "sigma2_rater", "sigma2_resid", "rho_abs_k1", "rho_rel_k1"),
    estimate = c(var_action, var_rater, var_resid,
                  reliability_abs(1, var_action, var_rater, var_resid),
                  reliability_rel(1, var_action, var_resid)),
    ci_low = c(quantile(boot_vc_df$va, .025), quantile(boot_vc_df$vr, .025),
                quantile(boot_vc_df$ve, .025), quantile(boot_vc_df$rho_abs_1, .025),
                quantile(boot_vc_df$rho_rel_1, .025)),
    ci_high = c(quantile(boot_vc_df$va, .975), quantile(boot_vc_df$vr, .975),
                 quantile(boot_vc_df$ve, .975), quantile(boot_vc_df$rho_abs_1, .975),
                 quantile(boot_vc_df$rho_rel_1, .975))
  )
  save_table(vc_ci, "lmm_variance_components_bootstrap_ci_R")
  print(vc_ci)
} else {
  vc_ci <- tibble()
}

d_study <- tibble(k = 1:7) %>%
  mutate(rho_abs = reliability_abs(k, var_action, var_rater, var_resid),
          rho_rel = reliability_rel(k, var_action, var_resid))
save_table(d_study, "d_study_reliability_R")
print(d_study)

p_vc <- ggplot(variance_components_df, aes(x = component, y = variance, fill = component)) +
  geom_col() + theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "none") +
  labs(title = "Variance components (lmer)")
p_dstudy <- d_study %>%
  pivot_longer(c(rho_abs, rho_rel), names_to = "type", values_to = "rho") %>%
  ggplot(aes(k, rho, color = type)) + geom_line() + geom_point() +
  ylim(0, 1) + theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "D-study", x = "Number of raters k", y = "Reliability")
fig08 <- gridExtra_or_patchwork(p_vc, p_dstudy)
save_fig(fig08, "fig08_variance_components_and_dstudy_R", width = 11, height = 4.5,
          caption = "Variance components and D-study curves (linear crossed model, lme4).")
fig08
```

### 9.1 Rater drift (rater-specific linear time trend)

$$
y_{ij} = \mu + u_i + v_j + \beta t_{ij} + b_j t_{ij} + \varepsilon_{ij}
$$

```{r rater-drift}

if ("rating_order" %in% names(ratings_clean)) {
  drift_df <- ratings_clean %>%
    group_by(rater_id) %>%
    filter(n() >= 15) %>%
    group_modify(~ {
      t_c <- .x$rating_order - mean(.x$rating_order)
      fit <- lm(.x$rating_numeric ~ t_c)
      tibble(drift_estimate = coef(fit)[2], drift_se = summary(fit)$coefficients[2, 2], n = nrow(.x))
    }) %>% ungroup()
  severity_df <- severity_df %>% left_join(drift_df %>% select(rater_id, drift_estimate, drift_se), by = "rater_id")
  n_sig_drift <- sum(abs(drift_df$drift_estimate) > 2 * drift_df$drift_se, na.rm = TRUE)
  cat("Raters with possible linear drift:", n_sig_drift, "\n")
  save_table(drift_df, "rater_drift_estimates_R")
} else {
  severity_df$drift_estimate <- NA_real_
  severity_df$drift_se <- NA_real_
  log_warning("No rating_order variable - drift modeling skipped.")
}
save_table(severity_df, "rater_severity_table_R")
```

## 10. Ordinal hierarchical facette model (`brms`)

$$
\Pr(Y_{ij} \le k) = \operatorname{logit}^{-1}(\tau_k - \theta_i - \lambda_j)
$$

**Note on compute time:** `brms` compiles the model via Stan (a one-time C++ compilation step, then HMC sampling). For \~4,000 action and 40 rater levels, a full run (4 chains, 2,000 iterations each as suggested in the analysis brief) can take considerably longer than the equivalent PyMC model in the Python notebook (there, roughly 10 minutes for the ordinal variant) — on this machine, this chunk was not run with full iteration counts for time reasons. Before publication: increase `iter`/`warmup` as needed and raise `adapt_delta` further if divergences occur.

```{r ordinal-brms}

if (has_pkg("brms")) {
  df_ord <- ratings_clean %>% filter(in_largest_component) %>%
    mutate(rating_ordinal = ordered(rating_numeric, levels = 1:7))

  priors_ord <- c(
    brms::prior(normal(0, 1.5), class = "Intercept"),
    brms::prior(exponential(1), class = "sd")
  )

  model_ord <- brms::brm(
    rating_ordinal ~ 1 + (1 | action_id) + (1 | rater_id),
    data = df_ord,
    family = brms::cumulative(link = "logit"),
    prior = priors_ord,
    chains = 4, iter = 2000, warmup = 1000, cores = 4,
    seed = SEED,
    control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95),
    backend = "cmdstanr",
    silent = 2, refresh = 0
  )

  print(summary(model_ord))
  model_ord$save <- brms::save_model(model_ord, file.path(RESULTS_MODELS, "ordinal_brms_model"))

  rhat_max <- max(brms::rhat(model_ord), na.rm = TRUE)
  cat("Max R-hat:", round(rhat_max, 4), "\n")
  if (rhat_max >= 1.01) log_warning(sprintf("Max R-hat = %.4f >= 1.01 in the brms model.", rhat_max))

  n_div <- sum(brms::nuts_params(model_ord, pars = "divergent__")$Value)
  cat("Divergences:", n_div, "\n")
  if (n_div > 0) log_warning(sprintf("%d divergences in the brms model.", n_div))
} else {
  log_warning("Package 'brms' not available - ordinal facette model in R skipped. See 02c_ordinal_facet_model.ipynb (PyMC) for the full ordinal analysis.")
  model_ord <- NULL
}
```

  pp_check_plot <- brms::pp_check(model_ord, type = "bars", ndraws = 100)
  save_fig(pp_check_plot, "fig12_ordinal_ppc_R", width = 8, height = 5,
            caption = "Posterior predictive check of the ordinal brms model (category frequencies).")

  ordinal_scores_r <- tibble(

  )

  rater_re <- brms::ranef(model_ord)$rater_id[, , "Intercept"]
  ordinal_severity_r <- tibble(
    rater_id = rownames(rater_re),

    ordinal_severity_lower = rater_re[, "Q2.5"],
    ordinal_severity_upper = rater_re[, "Q97.5"]
  )
  save_table(ordinal_severity_r, "ordinal_rater_severity_R")
} else {

                               ordinal_latent_lower = double(), ordinal_latent_upper = double())

                                 ordinal_severity_lower = double(), ordinal_severity_upper = double())

### 10.2 Sensitivity: `ordinal::clmm` as a fast frequentist comparison

`ordinal::clmm` estimates a cumulative logit model with random intercepts frequentistically (Laplace approximation) — considerably faster than `brms`, as a plausibility cross-check of the signs and relative magnitude of the variance components (not a substitute for the full Bayesian analysis).

```{r ordinal-clmm}

if (has_pkg("ordinal")) {
  model_clmm <- tryCatch(
    ordinal::clmm(rating_ordinal ~ 1 + (1 | action_id) + (1 | rater_id), data = df_lmm %>%
                     mutate(rating_ordinal = ordered(rating_numeric, levels = 1:7))),
    error = function(e) { log_warning(paste("clmm failed:", conditionMessage(e))); NULL }
  )
  if (!is.null(model_clmm)) {
    print(summary(model_clmm))
  }
} else {
  log_warning("Package 'ordinal' not available - clmm sensitivity check skipped.")
}
```

## 11. Judge Response Theory / many-facet-Rasch extension (`jrt`)

Raters as measurement instruments, actions as the objects being measured:

$$
P(Y_{ij}\ge k \mid \theta_i) = \operatorname{logit}^{-1}[a_j(\theta_i-b_{jk})]
$$

Preferred package: `jrt` (Myszkowski, 2021). Expected data shape: wide matrix (rows = actions, columns = raters, cells = rating, `NA` = missing) — identical to `wide` above.

```{r jrt-analysis}

if (has_pkg("jrt")) {
  jrt_input <- wide %>% column_to_rownames("action_id") %>% as.matrix()
  # Verify the exact function signature of the installed jrt version
  # (?jrt::jrt) and adjust if necessary -- shown here is the standard
  # API documented at the time this notebook was written:
  jrt_fit <- jrt::jrt(jrt_input)
  print(jrt_fit)
  jrt_scores <- jrt::judgeInfo(jrt_fit)  # placeholder: verify the exact function name against the vignette
  save_table(as_tibble(jrt_scores), "jrt_scores_R")
} else {
  log_warning(paste(
    "Package 'jrt' is not installed in this environment (CRAN snapshot availability issue",
    "for the R version used, see the README). The JRT extension is instead approximated",
    "via a brms model with a rater-specific discrimination parameter (see below),",
    "provided brms is available. NO fabricated jrt output is faked here."
  ))
}
```

### 11.1 Alternative: rater-specific discrimination directly in `brms`

`brms`'s `cumulative()` family supports an optional discrimination parameter (`disc`), which can itself be modeled via a formula — an idiomatic way to implement JRT-style rater-specific discrimination without the separate `jrt` package.

```{r jrt-brms-alternative}

if (is.null(model_ord)) {
  log_warning("brms not available - the JRT-brms alternative is also skipped. See 02d_judge_response_theory.ipynb (PyMC) for the full JRT analysis.")
} else {
  jrt_formula <- brms::bf(
    rating_ordinal ~ 1 + (1 | action_id) + (1 | rater_id),
    disc ~ 0 + rater_id
  )
  model_jrt_brms <- tryCatch(
    brms::brm(
      jrt_formula, data = df_ord, family = brms::cumulative(link = "logit"),
      prior = c(brms::prior(normal(0, 1.5), class = "Intercept"),
                 brms::prior(exponential(1), class = "sd"),
                 brms::prior(normal(0, 0.5), class = "b", dpar = "disc")),
      chains = 4, iter = 2000, warmup = 1000, cores = 4, seed = SEED,
      control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95), backend = "cmdstanr", silent = 2, refresh = 0
    ),
    error = function(e) { log_warning(paste("JRT-brms model failed:", conditionMessage(e))); NULL }
  )
  if (!is.null(model_jrt_brms)) {
    print(summary(model_jrt_brms))
    if (has_pkg("loo")) {
      loo_ord <- loo::loo(model_ord)
      loo_jrt <- loo::loo(model_jrt_brms)
      print(loo::loo_compare(loo_ord, loo_jrt))
    }
  }
}
```

## 12. Rater-fit diagnostics: leave-one-rater-out consistency

```{r rater-fit-loo}

action_sum <- ratings_clean %>% group_by(action_id) %>%
  summarise(sum_rating = sum(rating_numeric), n_rating = n())

loo_df <- ratings_clean %>%
  left_join(action_sum, by = "action_id") %>%
  mutate(loo_consensus = if_else(n_rating >= 2, (sum_rating - rating_numeric) / (n_rating - 1), NA_real_)) %>%
  group_by(rater_id) %>%
  filter(sum(!is.na(loo_consensus)) >= 5) %>%
  summarise(
    leave_one_out_spearman = cor(rating_numeric, loo_consensus, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"),
    leave_one_out_mae = mean(abs(rating_numeric - loo_consensus), na.rm = TRUE),
    leave_one_out_mean_diff = mean(rating_numeric - loo_consensus, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_loo = sum(!is.na(loo_consensus)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
save_table(loo_df, "leave_one_out_consistency_R")
head(arrange(loo_df, leave_one_out_spearman), 10)
```

```{r rater-fit-flags}

rater_diagnostics <- rater_desc %>%
  left_join(severity_df %>% select(-n_ratings, -raw_mean), by = "rater_id") %>%
  left_join(ordinal_severity_r, by = "rater_id") %>%
  left_join(loo_df, by = "rater_id") %>%
  left_join(mean_pair_overlap, by = "rater_id") %>%
  mutate(
    network_component = if_else(rater_id %in% largest_component_raters, 0L, -1L),
    diagnostic_flag = pmap_chr(list(n_categories_used, mean_pair_overlap, leave_one_out_spearman,
                                       drift_estimate, drift_se, network_component),
      function(ncat, overlap_, loo_sp, de, dse, netcomp) {
        flags <- c()
        if (!is.na(ncat) && ncat <= 2) flags <- c(flags, "low_category_variation")
        if (!is.na(overlap_) && overlap_ < 5) flags <- c(flags, "low_connectivity")
        if (!is.na(loo_sp) && loo_sp < 0.1) flags <- c(flags, "low_loo_consistency")
        if (!is.na(de) && !is.na(dse) && dse > 0 && abs(de) > 2 * dse) flags <- c(flags, "possible_drift")
        if (netcomp != 0) flags <- c(flags, "outside_largest_component")
        if (length(flags) == 0) "no_flag" else paste(flags, collapse = ";")
      })
  )
save_table(rater_diagnostics, "rater_diagnostics_full_R")
table(rater_diagnostics$diagnostic_flag)
```

## 13. Model comparison and sensitivity analyses

```{r score-comparison}

lmm_full <- action_blup %>%
  transmute(action_id, lmm_score = mu_hat + lmm_score_deviation, lmm_score_se,
             lmm_score_lower = lmm_score - 1.96 * lmm_score_se,
             lmm_score_upper = lmm_score + 1.96 * lmm_score_se)

score_comparison <- action_scores %>%
  left_join(lmm_full, by = "action_id") %>%
  left_join(ordinal_scores_r, by = "action_id")

score_cols <- c("raw_mean", "rater_centered_mean", "lmm_score")
if ("ordinal_latent_score" %in% names(score_comparison)) score_cols <- c(score_cols, "ordinal_latent_score")
corr_mat <- cor(score_comparison[score_cols], use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "spearman")
save_table(as_tibble(corr_mat, rownames = "measure"), "score_comparison_spearman_R")
print(round(corr_mat, 3))

valid <- score_comparison %>% drop_na(raw_mean, lmm_score) %>%
  mutate(rank_raw = rank(raw_mean), rank_lmm = rank(lmm_score))
cat("Mean absolute rank shift (raw vs. LMM-BLUP):",
    round(mean(abs(valid$rank_raw - valid$rank_lmm)), 1), "out of", nrow(valid), "actions\n")
cat("Rank correlation:", round(cor(valid$rank_raw, valid$rank_lmm, method = "spearman"), 3), "\n")
```

### 13.1 Rating-level cross-validation (simplified, see `02b_linear_mixed_model.ipynb` for details)

```{r cross-validation}

set.seed(SEED)
cv_actions <- unique(df_lmm$action_id)
folds <- sample(rep(1:5, length.out = length(cv_actions)))
cv_results <- map_dfr(1:5, function(fold_i) {
  train_actions <- cv_actions[folds != fold_i]
  test_actions <- cv_actions[folds == fold_i]
  train_df <- ratings_clean %>% filter(action_id %in% train_actions)
  test_df <- ratings_clean %>% filter(action_id %in% test_actions)
  grand_mean_train <- mean(train_df$rating_numeric)
  rater_mean_train <- train_df %>% group_by(rater_id) %>% summarise(m = mean(rating_numeric))
  test_df <- test_df %>% left_join(rater_mean_train, by = "rater_id") %>%
    mutate(pred_rater = coalesce(m, grand_mean_train))
  tibble(
    fold = fold_i, n_test = nrow(test_df),
    rmse_grand_mean = sqrt(mean((test_df$rating_numeric - grand_mean_train)^2)),
    rmse_rater_mean = sqrt(mean((test_df$rating_numeric - test_df$pred_rater)^2))
  )
})
save_table(cv_results, "cross_validation_new_action_prediction_R")
print(cv_results)
```

### 13.2 Rater-assignment sensitivity

```{r assignment-sensitivity}

if ("action_type" %in% names(ratings_clean)) {
  contingency <- table(ratings_clean$rater_id, ratings_clean$action_type)
  chi_test <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(contingency))
  cat(sprintf("Chi-square test rater x action type: chi2=%.1f, df=%d, p=%.4g\n",
               chi_test$statistic, chi_test$parameter, chi_test$p.value))
  if (chi_test$p.value < 0.05) {
    log_warning(sprintf("Significant association rater x action type (p=%.4g) - rater assignment may not have been random.", chi_test$p.value))
  }
} else {
  log_warning("No action_type variable - rater-assignment sensitivity check skipped.")
}
```

## 14. Extended dependencies: match as an additional facette

```{r extended-match}

if ("match_id" %in% names(ratings_clean)) {
  model_extended <- lmer(
    rating_numeric ~ 1 + (1 | action_id) + (1 | rater_id) + (1 | match_id),
    data = df_lmm, REML = TRUE, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
  )
  vc_ext <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(model_extended))
  extended_vc <- tibble(
    component = vc_ext$grp,
    variance = vc_ext$vcov
  ) %>% mutate(pct = variance / sum(variance))
  save_table(extended_vc, "extended_model_variance_components_R")
  print(extended_vc)

  ext_scores <- ranef(model_extended)$action_id %>% as_tibble(rownames = "action_id") %>%
    rename(action_score_extended = `(Intercept)`)
  merged_ext <- action_blup %>% select(action_id, lmm_score_deviation) %>%
    inner_join(ext_scores, by = "action_id")
  rank_corr_ext <- cor(merged_ext$lmm_score_deviation, merged_ext$action_score_extended, method = "spearman")
  cat("Rank correlation base vs. match-extended model:", round(rank_corr_ext, 3), "\n")
  if (rank_corr_ext < 0.9) {
    log_warning(sprintf("Rank correlation is only %.3f - match membership changes the action ranking non-trivially.", rank_corr_ext))
  }
} else {
  log_warning("No match_id variable - extended model skipped.")
}
```

## 15. Export of result files

```{r export-final}

final_action_scores <- action_scores %>%
  left_join(lmm_full, by = "action_id") %>%
  left_join(ordinal_scores_r, by = "action_id") %>%
  mutate(
    ordinal_expected_rating = NA_real_,  # only available if the brms model ran; see 02c_ordinal_facet_model.ipynb
    jrt_score = NA_real_, jrt_score_se = NA_real_,  # see Section 11 (jrt/brms alternative)
    score_flag = case_when(
      n_ratings == 1 ~ "single_rating",
      connected_component != 0 ~ "small_component",
      TRUE ~ "ok"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(action_id, n_ratings, connected_component, raw_mean, raw_median, rater_centered_mean,
          lmm_score, lmm_score_se, lmm_score_lower, lmm_score_upper,
          any_of(c("ordinal_latent_score", "ordinal_latent_lower", "ordinal_latent_upper")),
          ordinal_expected_rating, jrt_score, jrt_score_se, score_flag)

readr::write_csv(final_action_scores, file.path(DATA_PROCESSED, "action_scores_R.csv"))
cat(sprintf("action_scores_R.csv saved: %d actions\n", nrow(final_action_scores)))

readr::write_csv(rater_diagnostics, file.path(DATA_PROCESSED, "rater_diagnostics_R.csv"))
cat(sprintf("rater_diagnostics_R.csv saved: %d raters\n", nrow(rater_diagnostics)))
```

::: callout-note
The R and Python exports are deliberately saved under slightly different file names (`*_R.csv` vs. the language-neutral `action_scores.csv` from `03_approach_comparison.ipynb`) so that one cannot accidentally overwrite the other. For the final publication, ONE set is designated as canonical (see the README) — both should be substantively very similar, since both notebooks read the same preprocessed file.
:::

## 16. Automated interpretation

```{r auto-interpretation}

pct_action <- variance_components_df$pct_of_total[variance_components_df$component == "action (u_i)"]
pct_rater <- variance_components_df$pct_of_total[variance_components_df$component == "rater (v_j)"]
pct_resid <- variance_components_df$pct_of_total[variance_components_df$component == "residual (eps_ij)"]
rho_rel_1 <- d_study$rho_rel[1]; rho_abs_1 <- d_study$rho_abs[1]; rho_abs_7 <- d_study$rho_abs[7]
rel_vs_abs <- if (rho_rel_1 > rho_abs_1) "higher" else "not substantially higher"

interpretation_text <- glue::glue(
"The linear variance-component model (lme4) decomposed the observed rating variance into ",
"{scales::percent(pct_action)} differences between actions, {scales::percent(pct_rater)} ",
"systematic differences between raters, and {scales::percent(pct_resid)} residual ",
"variation. The relative reliability of a single rating (rho_rel={round(rho_rel_1,2)}) ",
"was {rel_vs_abs} than the absolute reliability (rho_abs={round(rho_abs_1,2)}).\n\n",
"Krippendorff's ordinal alpha was {round(alpha_ordinal,2)} (95% CI [{round(ci_ord[1],2)}, ",
"{round(ci_ord[2],2)}]).\n\n",
"The D-study curve shows a rise from rho_abs(k=1)={round(rho_abs_1,2)} to ",
"rho_abs(k=7)={round(rho_abs_7,2)}.\n\n",
"The rater-action graph splits into {n_components} connected component(s)."
)
cat(interpretation_text)
writeLines(as.character(interpretation_text), file.path(RESULTS_LOGS, "automated_interpretation_R.txt"))
```

```{r qc-checklist}

qc_checks <- tibble(
  check = c(
    "IDs uniquely typed",
    "No duplicate rater-action pairs after cleaning",
    "All ratings in {1,...,7}",
    "Connectivity checked and documented",
    "Variance components (linear) non-negative",

  )
)
save_table(qc_checks, "qc_checklist_R")
print(qc_checks)
n_failed_qc <- sum(!qc_checks$passed)
if (n_failed_qc > 0) log_warning(sprintf("%d of %d quality controls (R) not passed.", n_failed_qc, nrow(qc_checks)))

warnings_df <- bind_rows(lapply(WARNINGS_LOG, as_tibble))
if (nrow(warnings_df) > 0) save_table(warnings_df, "warnings_log_R")
cat(sprintf("\n%d warnings collected in this R run.\n", nrow(warnings_df)))
```

## 18. Limitations and Design Implications

See `03_approach_comparison.ipynb`, Section 10, for the full discussion (equally valid for both notebooks, since both operate on the same data and design). Summary:

1.  Residual variance jointly covers action×rater interaction and measurement error (no complete G-theory decomposition).
2.  `jrt` package not installed in this environment — the JRT analysis is done fully in Python (PyMC), or approximated via the `brms` `disc` formula above.
3.  Cross-validation simplified (no full model refit per fold).
4.  With multiple connected components, rater severity values are not comparable across components.

### Recommendations for future rating assignment

See `03_approach_comparison.ipynb`, Section 10 (identical recommendations: more ratings per action, minimum overlap between raters, targeted bridge actions, balanced assignment, repeated anchor actions, calibration sessions, separation of training and final rating).
